text:
anya: Nightly kernel-ci finished. Saw a reproducible perf regression for candidate kernel `matmul-fused-v2` on AVX2 variants when sequence length >= 1024. Logs + microbench attached.

derek: Ugh, saw alert from perf-bot this morning. Is this across all batch sizes or just single-stream?

anya: Mainly single-stream and small batches (1-4). Throughput tests (large batches) look fine.

jeff: Can you paste the microbench command you ran?

anya: Reproducer I used:
```
./kernbench --kernel matmul-fused-v2 --arch avx2 --seq-len 2048 --batch 1 --iters 200 --profile
```
Results snippet: p50 per-token latency (ms): baseline `matmul-ref` = 1.8, candidate `matmul-fused-v2` = 2.6 (+45%). p95 baseline=2.4 vs candidate=3.9.

lin: That's huge for long seqs. Any KV cache weirdness?

anya: Yes — profiler shows a hot path in the fused kernel that does extra conditional checks on KV cache hits. Cold-cache path seems fine, but when KV entries are reused (typical long-seq workloads) branch mispredict + vector spill cost skyrockets. I attached the perf flamegraph: https://internal.redwood/perf/1854321000/flame.svg (private).

perf-bot: CI job `kernel-ci/67281` failed: longseq-avx2-suite — regression detected against rollout baseline.

derek: Could the autotuner be picking fused-v2 for seqlen buckets > 512 incorrectly? Our seqlen->kernel mapping has a boundary at 1024 but autotuner learned a preference from microbench noise.

anya: Exactly. The nightly autotune sweep's loss function weights throughput more than branch stability; for certain input distributions it favored fused-v2 on AVX2. Need to add a stability penalty for branch-heavy kernels on 'repeated-KV' workloads.

jeff: Proposal: 1) revert fused-v2 as default for AVX2 + seqlen >=1024 in the selector table, 2) augment autotuner feature set to include 'branchiness' metric from perf counters, 3) queue a focused nightly micro-sweep for seqlen buckets [512,1024,2048] with KV-reuse trace.

lin: I can file the revert PR. Quick patch: change selector_rule: `if arch==avx2 and seqlen>=1024 -> prefer matmul-ref` and mark fused-v2 as experimental for long sequences.

anya: Thanks. Also adding a short-term heuristic: if KV reuse ratio > 0.6, prefer tiled kernels. This lives in the runtime policy layer (not the autotuner) so it takes effect immediately.

derek: For the autotuner change, add perf counters: #branch-misses / #instructions as a scalar feature. Weight it with a penalty factor alpha. We'll need to retrain the model on nightly labels.

jeff: Action items:
- lin: PR to selector (revert) — ETA today EOD.
- anya: Create deterministic micro-sweep job with KV-reuse traces (job template `kernel-longseq-kv-sweep`) — ETA tomorrow.
- derek: Update autotuner features + training job (ticket AUTOTUNE-342) — ETA 3 days.
- ops-bot: hold rollout of `matmul-fused-v2` to Dedicated pools until we verify.

ops-bot: Rollout hold enacted for `matmul-fused-v2` in Dedicated (tagged).

anya: I'll post the raw perf counters here for the 2048 run:
```
cycles: 3.2e9
instructions: 7.6e9
branch-misses: 3.1e7
L1-dcache-loads: 1.2e8
vector-reg-spills: 412
```
Derived: branch-miss rate ~= 0.0041, vector-reg-spills correlated with latency spikes.

jeff: Good data. After the revert + heuristic, let's run the nightly sweep with both cold and hot KV traces and compare. If fused-v2 still wins on large-batch throughput we can keep it for batch>=16 only.

anya: Noted. I'll also attach the minimal repro harness (small script) to the autotune job so we don't need manual runs.

lin: PR submitted: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2391 — patch reverts selector for avx2 longseq. PTAL.

derek: LGTM, landing after CI passes.

anya: Thanks everyone — keeping this thread for follow-ups. If you see anomalies in perf-dashboard, @here. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
